messages.author: 1e955ab90bb687bc
messages.subject: Further strategies to deal with divergent transitions
parts:
Hi there! First of all, thank you for being awesome. I enjoy programming in Stan A LOT and I always read this mailing list hoping to learn something new.

I've got this little model full of divergent transitions. It's a GARCH(1, 1) model (as implemented in the manual) for K = 2 states where the transition probabilities are estimated by the forward algorithm. On a single run, the code estimates the parameters for n = 1, ..., N independent datasets. Please, find attached my fully working code and an output summary so you don't have to run it yourself. The estimates make sense at first glance, but I was warned that they are biased. As stated by Intergalactic Betan Policies, they shouldn't be trusted. I first thought the sampler is having a hard time at estimating parameters for N independent datasets, but I made the model collapse to N = 1 and had the same problem. Also, I'd like to keep everything together so I can add some hierarchical magic later.

After long reading this mailing list, I've learnt my posterior is misbehaved and the sampler walks clumsily along the curvature, taking steps so big it won't discover the details of the surface. Usually, three strategies are discussed: (1) force the sampling take smaller steps by increasing adapt_delta and decreasing stepsize, (2) add prior information to smooth the posterior curvature, and (3) reparametrise. The first step will help mostly with divergences on the upper diagonal of the pairs plot. In my case, it solved part of the problem, leaving 250/1600 divergences when adapt_delta = 0.99 and stepsize = 0.01. For step two, unfortunately I don't have many parameters in my models. Even more, most them are highly constrained (namely 0 < alpha1 <= 1, beta1 => 0, alpha1+beta1 < 1, p0 and TP are probabilities with 0 <= p <= 1). Basically, there's not much room for priors. For the last step, well, my model is pretty simple so I don't know how to reparametrise this prima facie.

Being stuck, I can only send the distress signal and ask the savvy what other strategies you'd suggest. Do you see something suspicious in my code? Maybe some snippet that smells bad? S.O.S.

Regards,

Luis.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Further strategies to deal with divergent transitions
parts:
First of all, you don't need these epsilon lower bounds:

real<lower=0.00000001> nu;

If your estimates for nu are getting that close to zero, there's
a problem with your model. In that case, we recommend priors rather
than these hard constraints.

In general, constraining parameters can make the fitting much much
harder if the unconstrained parameter would sample beyond the
constraint boundary. What happens is that on the unconstrained scale
is that Stan has to explore out to plus or minus infinity to get
some draws. And it biases the outcome.

I don't understand your model, but those exp(normal_lpdf(...)) can
be bad news due to underflow. I'd suggest keeping everything on
the log scale.

Is that likelihood a mixture model? Otherwise, I don't understand
why you're using log_sum_exp over T rather than sum.

Ther'es a lot of thing syou can vectorize as well, but that's just
an efficiency issue.

- Bob
